text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed canary telemetry and quota attribution diverging after the new route-attr shim landed in the Python/TS clients. Console shows a ~30% higher quota burn for a handful of tenants.

maria: Which shim? the one that moves route metadata into `x-rd-route`?

alex: Yeah — exactly. Repro: 1) call hosted API with legacy `Route-ID` header 2) client-side shim translates into `x-rd-route: {id,priority}` 3) console mapping appears to treat that as a separate route id for quota ledger.

jamal: Oof. Is the console ingest normalizing header keys? We recently added a sampling path that groups by header name + hash.

nora: Paging the runtime team — this could be an attribution mismatch between ingest and the quota service. We changed the canonical ID earlier this quarter.

infra-bot: deploy/ingest-service v2.14 -> prod (canary) triggered by @alex at 2026-03-22T18:02:11Z :rocket:

maria: Can you post a minimal curl that reproduces? if we can hit the same flow we can confirm where it diverges.

alex: Minimal snippet: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Route-ID: my-tenant-42" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` — client shim (py/ts) will convert to `x-rd-route` on the wire.

jamal: I ran that against canary and saw two different `route_key` fields in logs: one from meter-proxy and one from ingest. meter-proxy shows `route_key=my-tenant-42` but ingest shows `route_key=hash:abcd1234` (because it used the hashed x-rd-route canonicalizer).

nora: That explains the quota mismatch — quota ledger indexes on the unhashed ID, console groups on hashed fingerprint. Quick fix options: 1) align ingest to use unhashed route key, 2) change quota ledger to accept hashed keys and map back, 3) shim at console to merge keys for the canary window.

maria: Option 3 is lowest risk for canary. We can add a transient mapping table in the console tile that maps hashed keys -> original header while canary is active. We'll need the mapping ID pairs.

alex: I can produce a csv of observed (Route-ID -> hashed) from the canary logs. Will share in #eng-runtime once ready.

jamal: For SDKs: we pushed a minor that enabled the shim by default. Should we flip that to opt-in until we confirm backend behavior?

nora: Yes please. Rollback toggle recommended. We should feature-flag the shim across languages and stop defaulting it on until ingestion is stable.

console: We'll add a console-side reconciliation job and a dashboard panel showing dual-key counts (hashed vs unhashed) and a checkbox to merge. Also will add an annotation on the tenant flyout indicating their traffic may be double-counted during canary.

alex: Action items: 1) @jamal revert py/ts default to opt-in (cut a patch) 2) @maria add console reconciliation and temporary mapping UI 3) @nora coordinate ingest -> meter-proxy canonicalization alignment 4) alex to upload mapping csv. Target: freeze defaults within 24h, reconciliation live within 48h.

maria: I'll scope the console change and prep a canary dashboard.

jamal: Preparing a patch branch now: `fix/shim-opt-in` — will open PR and link here.

nora: I'll run a small end-to-end test once jamal's patch is up. If clean, we can re-enable gradual opt-in and add a telemetry metric to detect divergence under 5% before defaulting on.

alex: Thanks all. Quick note — keep any tenant-facing language conservative; we'll mark it as \"internal canary artifact\" until reconciled. :white_check_mark:
